title: Spanish club outspends City in the Champions League
seoTitle: Spanish club outspends City in Champions League
subtitle: Real Madrid leads the spending race in the current season
excerpt: Real Madrid and Barcelona have already spent over $200 million on signings, even outspending Manchester City.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Real Madrid has already spent over 200 million dollars on signings, even surpassing Manchester City, which has the highest total investment of around 610 million dollars. While Real Madrid and Barcelona are among the clubs that spent the most this season, Manchester City leads the global spending ranking, but still falls behind the two Spanish giants.

Spanish club leads transfer spending

The Spanish clubs participating in the Champions League group stage include Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atlético Madrid, Villarreal, and Real Betis. Real Madrid invested in Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konaté, Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Yan Diomande, and Carlos Espí, totaling around 261 million dollars. Barcelona, for its part, spent approximately 213 million dollars, including the arrival of Rodri.

Comparison with Manchester City

Manchester City is the club that has invested the most this season, with the signings of Elliott Anderson, Enzo Fernández, and Ayoub Bouaddi, totaling 610 million dollars. This figure makes City Europe's biggest investor, but it still lags behind Real Madrid in terms of spending.

Impact on European campaigns

Real Madrid enters the competition after being eliminated in the quarter-final stage last season and looks to rejoin the fight for the title. Barcelona, which missed out on last season, is trying to close the gap on Europe's elite clubs. Atlético Madrid, although not one of the biggest spenders, relies on new signings like Cristian Romero and Jonathan David to strengthen their squad.

Expectations of Spanish clubs

Real Betis, in its first appearance in over 20 years, hopes to advance to the knockout stages. Villarreal seeks to improve its group stage campaign, which ended with just one point. Atlético Madrid, which claimed the World Cup title in 2010, looks to regain form after a 3-0 defeat to Athletic Bilbao.

Competition format remains the same

The Champions League format remains unchanged: each team plays eight games in the group stage, with four matches at home and four away. The top 8 in the table advance directly to the round of 16, while teams ranked 9th to 24th play a playoff to decide the final spots in the knockout stage.
